description: Registry of measurement instruments for human responses to built environments

instruments.authors: Spielberger, C. D., Gorsuch, R. L., Lushene, R., Vagg, P. R., & Jacobs, G. A.
instruments.reference_apa: Spielberger, C. D. (1983). State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI). Consulting Psychologists Press.
instruments.description: 40-item self-report measure of state and trait anxiety. Respondents rate items on 4-point scales regarding presence of anxiety symptoms and worry.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Strong convergent and discriminant validity. Extensively validated across populations.

instruments.authors: Spitzer, R. L., Kroenke, K., Williams, J. B., & Löwe, B.
instruments.reference_apa: Spitzer, R. L., Kroenke, K., Williams, J. B., & Löwe, B. (2006). A brief measure for assessing generalized anxiety disorder. Archives of Internal Medicine, 166(10), 1092-1097.
instruments.description: 7-item self-report screening tool for generalized anxiety disorder. Rapid assessment in clinical and research settings.

psychometrics.validity_notes: High sensitivity (0.89) and specificity (0.97) for GAD diagnosis.

instruments.authors: Lovibond, S. H., & Lovibond, P. F.
instruments.reference_apa: Lovibond, S. H., & Lovibond, P. F. (1995). Manual for the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (2nd ed.). Psychology Foundation of Australia.
instruments.description: 21-item self-report measure of depression, anxiety, and stress. Three subscales (7 items each) assess negative emotional states.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Good discriminant validity across subscales.

instruments.authors: Watson, D., Clark, L. A., & Tellegen, A.
instruments.reference_apa: Watson, D., Clark, L. A., & Tellegen, A. (1988). Development and validation of brief measures of positive and negative affect. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 54(6), 1063-1070.
instruments.description: 20-item self-report of positive and negative affective states. Two 10-item subscales assess momentary emotional experience.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Well-established factor structure for positive and negative affect.

instruments.authors: Bradley, M. M., & Lang, P. J.
instruments.reference_apa: Bradley, M. M., & Lang, P. J. (1994). Measuring emotion. Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry, 25(1), 49-59.
instruments.description: Non-verbal pictorial scale assessing valence, arousal, and dominance in response to stimuli. Graphical manikin figures represent emotional dimensions.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Good convergent validity with physiological measures of arousal.

instruments.authors: McNair, D. M., Lorr, M., & Droppleman, L. F.
instruments.reference_apa: McNair, D. M., Lorr, M., & Droppleman, L. F. (1971). Manual for the Profile of Mood States. Educational and Industrial Testing Service.
instruments.description: 65-item self-report of mood across six dimensions: tension, depression, anger, vigor, fatigue, confusion.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Well-validated across clinical and non-clinical populations.

instruments.authors: Cohen, S., Kamarck, T., & Mermelstein, R.
instruments.reference_apa: Cohen, S., Kamarck, T., & Mermelstein, R. (1983). A global measure of perceived stress. Journal of Health and Social Behavior, 24(4), 385-396.
instruments.description: 10-item self-report of perceived stress over past month. Assesses degree to which situations feel uncontrollable and overwhelming.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Good convergent validity with health outcomes.

instruments.authors: Wewers, M. E., & Lowe, N. K.
instruments.reference_apa: Wewers, M. E., & Lowe, N. K. (1990). A critical review of visual analogue scale (VAS) for the measurement of clinical phenomena. Research in Nursing and Health, 13(4), 227-236.
instruments.description: Generic continuous scale (typically 0-100mm or 0-10) for rating affective or pain states. Flexible for various constructs.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Validity depends on specific application and anchors.

instruments.authors: Hartig, T., Korpela, K., Evans, G. W., & Gärling, T.
instruments.reference_apa: Hartig, T., Korpela, K., Evans, G. W., & Gärling, T. (1997). A measure of restorative quality in environments. Scandinavian Housing and Planning Research, 14(4), 175-194.
instruments.description: 26-item self-report measuring perceived restorative qualities of environments. Four subscales: being away, fascination, coherence, scope.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates with attention restoration theory predictions.

instruments.reference_apa: Korpela, K. M., & Hartig, T. (2008). Restorative quality of favorite places. Journal of Environmental Psychology, 28(2), 157-165.
instruments.description: 7-item self-report of perceived restorative outcomes from environments. Shorter alternative to PRS focusing on restoration perceptions.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Efficient brief measure with good psychometric properties.

instruments.reference_apa: Lyubomirsky, S., & Lepper, H. S. (1999). A measure of subjective happiness. Journal of Personality Assessment, 72(2), 169-194.
instruments.description: 4-item self-report of overall happiness and life satisfaction. Direct assessment of subjective well-being.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Valid across cultures and populations.

instruments.authors: Yaden, D. B., Iwry, J., Slack, K. J., Eichstaedt, J. C., Zhao, Y., Vaillant, G. E., & Newberg, A. B.
instruments.reference_apa: Yaden, D. B., Iwry, J., Slack, K. J., et al. (2019). The Awe Experience Scale. Journal of Positive Psychology, 14(4), 474-488.
instruments.description: 12-item self-report measuring awe responses to stimuli or environments. Captures vastness, accommodation, and affect dimensions.

psychometrics.validity_notes: New measure with emerging empirical support.

instruments.reference_apa: Ekman, P., & Friesen, W. V. (1978). Facial Action Coding System: A technique for the measurement of facial movement. Consulting Psychologists Press.
instruments.description: Systematic coding of facial action units. Observer-rated measure of emotions expressed via facial muscle movements.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Gold standard for facial emotion assessment.

instruments.reference_apa: Csikszentmihalyi, M. (1987). The systematic assessment of flow in daily experience. Journal of Happiness Studies, 1(1), 25-46.
instruments.description: Ecological momentary assessment protocol. Participants report emotions, activities, and context multiple times daily using pagers or smartphones.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Reduces recall bias and captures real-time experience.

instruments.authors: Kahneman, D., Krueger, A. B., Schkade, D. A., Schwarz, N., & Stone, A. A.
instruments.reference_apa: Kahneman, D., Krueger, A. B., Schkade, D. A., et al. (2004). A survey method for characterizing daily life experience. Science, 306(5702), 1776-1780.
instruments.description: Retrospective protocol where respondents reconstruct previous day's activities and associated affect. Captures hedonic well-being over full day.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Good convergent validity with ESM and physiological measures.

instruments.authors: Connor, K. M., & Davidson, J. R.
instruments.reference_apa: Connor, K. M., & Davidson, J. R. (2003). Development of a new resilience scale. Depression and Anxiety, 18(2), 76-82.
instruments.description: 25-item self-report of resilience and ability to cope with adversity. Five subscales assess personal competence, trust, adaptation.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Valid for trauma, depression, and general populations.

instruments.authors: Smith, B. W., Dalen, J., Wiggins, K., Tooley, E., Christopher, P., & Bernard, J.
instruments.reference_apa: Smith, B. W., Dalen, J., Wiggins, K., et al. (2008). The Brief Resilience Scale. Journal of Health Psychology, 13(2), 233-243.
instruments.description: 6-item self-report measuring ability to bounce back from stress. Very brief assessment of resilience.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Valid across diverse populations.

instruments.reference_apa: Leaman, R., & Summers, R. (2001). Bupleurum and emotional experience. Journal of Environmental Psychology, 21(4), 381-393.
instruments.description: Brief unpleasantness scale assessing negative affect in specific environmental contexts.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Limited empirical validation in current literature.

instruments.authors: Daniel, T. C., & Boster, R. S.
instruments.reference_apa: Daniel, T. C., & Boster, R. S. (1976). Measuring landscape esthetics. Land Economics, 52(3), 307-322.
instruments.description: Semantic differential scale for rating environmental aesthetics and perceived quality across multiple dimensions.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Useful for environmental perception research.

instruments.authors: Russell, J. A., Weiss, A., & Mendelsohn, G. A.
instruments.reference_apa: Russell, J. A., Weiss, A., & Mendelsohn, G. A. (1989). Affect Grid. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 57(3), 493-502.
instruments.description: Single-item 9x9 grid capturing valence and arousal simultaneously. Efficient 2D affect measurement.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Valid for momentary affect assessment.

instruments.reference_apa: Williams, L. A., & DeSteno, D. (2003). Positive affect facets. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 87(2), 169-186.
instruments.description: 10-item self-report measuring positive emotional states. Focused assessment of positive affect quality.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates well with approach motivation and well-being.

instruments.authors: Fan, J., McCandliss, B. D., Sommer, T., Raz, A., & Posner, M. I.
instruments.reference_apa: Fan, J., McCandliss, B. D., Sommer, T., Raz, A., & Posner, M. I. (2002). The activation of attentional networks. NeuroImage, 26(2), 471-479.
instruments.description: Flanker-based computerized task measuring three attention networks: alerting, orienting, and executive control.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Measures three dissociable attention systems.

instruments.authors: Rosvold, H. E., Mirsky, A. F., Sarason, I., Bransome, E. D., & Beck, L. H.
instruments.reference_apa: Rosvold, H. E., Mirsky, A. F., Sarason, I., et al. (1956). A continuous performance test of brain damage. Journal of Consulting Psychology, 20(5), 343-350.
instruments.description: Sustained attention task where participants respond to target stimuli amid distractors over extended period. Classic vigilance measure.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Sensitive to attentional deficits and psychopathology.

instruments.reference_apa: Stroop, J. R. (1935). Studies of interference in serial verbal reactions. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 18(6), 643-662.
instruments.description: Executive function task requiring suppression of automatic responses. Color names printed in incongruent colors require naming the ink color while inhibiting word reading.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Classic measure of executive function and cognitive control.

instruments.authors: Eriksen, C. W., & Eriksen, B. A.
instruments.reference_apa: Eriksen, C. W., & Eriksen, B. A. (1974). Effects of noise letters upon the identification of a target letter in a nonsearch task. Perception & Psychophysics, 16(1), 143-149.
instruments.description: Selective attention task using directional arrows surrounded by congruent/incongruent distractors. Measures conflict monitoring and resolution.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Sensitive to attention and executive control processes.

instruments.authors: Robertson, I. H., Manly, T., Andrade, J., Baddeley, B. T., & Yiend, J.
instruments.reference_apa: Robertson, I. H., Manly, T., Andrade, J., Baddeley, B. T., & Yiend, J. (1997). Oops!: Performance correlates of everyday attentional failures. Memory, 5(4), 515-524.
instruments.description: Frequent go-task with rare no-go trials measuring sustained attention and response inhibition. Sensitive to mind wandering.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Captures unintentional attention lapses.

instruments.authors: Dinges, D. F., & Powell, J. W.
instruments.reference_apa: Dinges, D. F., & Powell, J. W. (1985). Microcomputer analyses of performance on a portable, simple visual RT task during sustained operations. Behavior Research Methods, Instruments, & Computers, 17(6), 652-655.
instruments.description: Simple reaction-time task measuring vigilance and fatigue. Participants respond to random visual stimulus onsets over 10+ minutes.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Sensitive to fatigue and circadian variation.

instruments.reference_apa: Guilford, J. P. (1967). The Nature of Human Intelligence. McGraw-Hill.
instruments.description: Open-ended creativity task. Participants generate alternative uses for common objects (e.g., brick, paperclip).

psychometrics.validity_notes: Measures divergent thinking; scoring varies (fluency, flexibility, originality).

instruments.reference_apa: Mednick, S. A. (1962). The associative basis of the creative process. Psychological Review, 69(3), 220-232.
instruments.description: Convergent creativity task requiring finding common associates for three words. Measures insight and associative ability.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Valid measure of associative thinking and insight.

instruments.reference_apa: Torrance, E. P. (1966). Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking. Personnel Press.
instruments.description: Comprehensive creativity battery with verbal and figural subtests. Measures fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Extensively used in creativity research.

instruments.reference_apa: Reitan, R. M. (1958). Validity of the Trail Making Test as an indicator of organic brain damage. Perceptual and Motor Skills, 8(3), 271-276.
instruments.description: Two-part visuomotor task: Part A (connect numbers) and Part B (alternate numbers and letters). Measures attention, speed, and executive function.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Widely used screening for cognitive impairment.

instruments.reference_apa: Berg, E. A. (1948). A simple objective technique for measuring flexibility in thinking. Journal of General Psychology, 39(1), 15-22.
instruments.description: Executive function task requiring flexible rule application. Participants sort cards by color, shape, or number; sorting rule changes without announcement.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Measures cognitive flexibility and set-shifting.

instruments.reference_apa: Kirchner, W. K. (1958). Age differences in short-term retention of rapidly changing information. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 55(4), 352-358.
instruments.description: Working memory task requiring match detection between current and n-trials-back stimulus. Adaptable difficulty (1-back to 3-back typical).

psychometrics.validity_notes: Sensitive to working memory load.

instruments.authors: Turner, M. L., & Engle, R. W.
instruments.reference_apa: Turner, M. L., & Engle, R. W. (1989). Is working memory capacity task dependent? Journal of Memory and Language, 28(2), 127-154.
instruments.description: Complex span task interleaving math problems with word memory. Measures working memory capacity while engaging processing resources.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Predicts cognitive abilities and reasoning.

instruments.reference_apa: Rey, A. (1941). L'examen psychologique dans les cas d'encéphalopathie traumatique [Psychological examination in cases of traumatic encephalopathy]. Archives of Psychology, 28, 286-340.
instruments.description: Verbal learning and memory test. List of 15 words presented 5 times; measures learning curve, interference, and delayed recall.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Sensitive to memory impairment across conditions.

instruments.reference_apa: Raven, J. C. (1938). Raven's Progressive Matrices. H.K. Lewis & Co.
instruments.description: Non-verbal reasoning test using pattern matrices. Participants select missing element from multiple choices. Classic IQ measure.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Strong correlation with general intelligence (g).

instruments.authors: Hart, S. G., & Staveland, L. E.
instruments.reference_apa: Hart, S. G., & Staveland, L. E. (1988). Development of NASA-TLX (Task Load Index). Human Factors, 23(3), 239-250.
instruments.description: Self-report of perceived workload across six dimensions: mental demand, physical demand, temporal demand, effort, performance, frustration.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Valid predictor of task performance and demand.

instruments.authors: Broadbent, D. E., Cooper, P. F., FitzGerald, P., & Parkes, K. R.
instruments.reference_apa: Broadbent, D. E., Cooper, P. F., FitzGerald, P., & Parkes, K. R. (1982). The Cognitive Failures Questionnaire (CFQ). British Journal of Clinical Psychology, 21(1), 1-16.
instruments.description: 25-item self-report of everyday cognitive failures and slips. Measures attentional lapses and memory failures in daily life.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates with stress and sleep quality.

instruments.authors: Nasreddine, Z. S., Phillips, N. A., Bédirian, V., et al.
instruments.reference_apa: Nasreddine, Z. S., Phillips, N. A., Bédirian, V., et al. (2005). Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Journal of the American Geriatrics Society, 53(4), 695-699.
instruments.description: Rapid screening battery covering multiple cognitive domains: attention, language, visuospatial, memory, executive function, orientation.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Sensitive to mild cognitive impairment.

instruments.reference_apa: Smith, A. (1982). Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT). Western Psychological Services.
instruments.description: Rapid symbol-to-digit coding task. Measure of processing speed and visuomotor coordination. Simple but sensitive to cognitive decline.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Sensitive to MS, aging, and neurological conditions.

instruments.reference_apa: Navon, D. (1977). Forest before trees: The precedence of global features in visual perception. Cognitive Psychology, 9(3), 353-383.
instruments.description: Hierarchical stimulus perception task. Large letters composed of smaller letters require identification at different levels.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Assesses global vs. local processing bias.

instruments.reference_apa: Pylyshyn, Z., & Storm, R. W. (1988). Tracking multiple independent targets. Spatial Vision, 3(3), 179-197.
instruments.description: Attention-demanding task tracking multiple moving targets amid distractors. Measures attentional capacity.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Indexes attentional capacity limits.

instruments.reference_apa: Donders, F. C. (1868). Die Schnelligkeit psychischer Processe [The speed of mental processes]. Archiv für Anatomie und Physiologie, 657-681.
instruments.description: Response inhibition task. Participants respond to frequent go-stimuli but inhibit response to rare no-go stimuli.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Measures inhibitory control.

instruments.reference_apa: Logan, G. D. (1984). On the ability to inhibit thought and action. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 113(4), 644-654.
instruments.description: Go-reaction task with unpredictable stop-signal. Measures response inhibition latency and inhibitory control capacity.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Measures inhibitory control and impulsivity.

instruments.reference_apa: Shallice, T. (1982). Specific impairments of planning. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B, 298(1089), 199-209.
instruments.description: Planning and problem-solving task using three pegs and colored discs. Participants solve puzzles in minimum moves.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Measures planning and goal-directed behavior.

instruments.reference_apa: Einthoven, W. (1903). Die galvanometrische Registrierung des menschlichen Elektrokardiogramms [Galvanometric registration of the human electrocardiogram]. Pflügers Archiv, 99(3), 472-480.
instruments.description: Measurement of electrical heart activity. Records cardiac rhythm and detects arrhythmias. Portable devices available.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Gold standard for cardiac activity assessment.

instruments.reference_apa: Hertzman, A. B. (1937). Observations on the finger volume pulse recorded photoelectrically. American Journal of Physiology, 119(2), 334-335.
instruments.description: Non-invasive measurement of blood volume and heart rate using light absorption. Wearable finger/ear sensors available.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Valid for heart rate and heart rate variability.

instruments.reference_apa: Boucsein, W. (2012). Electrodermal Activity (2nd ed.). Springer.
instruments.description: Measurement of skin conductance in response to stimuli. Sensitive indicator of emotional arousal and autonomic activity.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Valid measure of emotional arousal.

instruments.reference_apa: Standard electrophysiology method for muscle activity measurement.
instruments.description: Measurement of electrical muscle activity. Detects muscle tension and movement. Facial EMG (corrugator, zygomatic) used in emotion research.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Valid for muscle activation and emotion expression.

instruments.reference_apa: Åkerstedt, T., & Gillberg, M. (1990). Subjective and objective sleepiness in the active individual. International Journal of Neuroscience, 52(1-2), 29-37.
instruments.description: 9-point self-report of momentary sleepiness. Rapid assessment of fatigue state in real-time or post-task.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates with objective alertness measures.

instruments.authors: Buysse, D. J., Reynolds III, C. F., Monk, T. H., Berman, S. R., & Kupfer, D. J.
instruments.reference_apa: Buysse, D. J., Reynolds III, C. F., Monk, T. H., Berman, S. R., & Kupfer, D. J. (1989). The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI): A new instrument for psychiatric practice and research. Psychiatry Research, 28(2), 193-213.
instruments.description: 19-item self-report measure of sleep quality and sleep disturbance. Assesses seven sleep components: sleep duration, latency, efficiency, disturbance, use of medication, daytime dysfunction, and sleep satisfaction.

psychometrics.validity_notes: High sensitivity (0.89) and specificity (0.86) for poor sleep quality.

instruments.authors: Chalder, T., Berelowitz, G., Pawlikowska, T., Wallace, P., Wessely, S., & Wright, D.
instruments.reference_apa: Chalder, T., Berelowitz, G., Pawlikowska, T., Wallace, P., Wessely, S., & Wright, D. (1993). Development of a fatigue scale. Journal of Psychosomatic Research, 37(2), 147-153.
instruments.description: 14-item self-report measure of physical and mental fatigue. Assesses subjective fatigue severity and impact on daily functioning.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Good convergent validity with objective fatigue measures.

strengths: Distinction between physical and cognitive fatigue
weaknesses: Limited normative data in non-clinical samples

instruments.reference_apa: Tyler, C. W. (1997). Human symmetry perception and its computational analysis. Journal of Physiology, 505(3), 617-626.
instruments.description: Psychophysical measure of the critical frequency at which a flickering light is perceived as continuous. Indicates visual processing speed and alertness.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates with EEG alpha and arousal state.

instruments.reference_apa: Melzack, R. (1975). The McGill Pain Questionnaire: Major properties and scoring methods. Pain, 1(3), 277-299.
instruments.description: 78-item multidimensional pain assessment tool. Evaluates sensory, affective, and evaluative dimensions of pain experience.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Well-validated across acute and chronic pain populations.

instruments.reference_apa: Scott, J., & Huskisson, E. C. (1976). Graphic representation of pain. Pain, 2(2), 175-184.
instruments.description: Single 100mm line anchored with 'no pain' and 'worst imaginable pain'. Respondent marks current pain level; rapid quantitative pain intensity assessment. Specific pain application of the Visual Analog Scale.

psychometrics.validity_notes: High correlations with other pain measures.

weaknesses: May underestimate pain in some populations

instruments.reference_apa: Fanger, P. O. (1972). Thermal Comfort: Analysis and Applications in Environmental Engineering. Danish Technical Press.
instruments.description: 7-point thermal sensation scale (-3 cold to +3 hot). Standard measure in thermal comfort research, derived from Fanger's PMV-PPD model.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Excellent agreement with physiological thermal markers.

weaknesses: Ordinal scale with potential non-linear spacing

instruments.full_name: Predicted Mean Vote - Predicted Percentage Dissatisfied
instruments.reference_apa: Fanger, P. O. (1970). Thermal Comfort: Analysis and Applications in Environmental Engineering. Danish Technical Press.
instruments.description: Predictive model combining metabolic rate, clothing, air temperature, mean radiant temperature, air velocity, and humidity to predict group thermal sensation and dissatisfaction.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Predictive accuracy decreases at temperature extremes.

weaknesses: Assumptions about metabolic rate and clothing

instruments.reference_apa: Sadeh, A., Hauri, P. J., Kripke, D. F., & Lavie, P. (1995). The role of actigraphy in the evaluation of sleep disorders. Sleep, 18(4), 288-302.
instruments.description: Wearable accelerometer measuring gross motor activity over extended periods. Continuous non-invasive assessment of sleep-wake patterns and circadian rhythm.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Moderate agreement with polysomnography for sleep classification; excellent for activity trends.

weaknesses: Cannot distinguish rest from quiet wakefulness

instruments.reference_apa: Beatty, J. (1982). Task-evoked pupillary responses, processing load, and the structure of processing resources. Psychological Bulletin, 91(2), 276-292.
instruments.description: Measurement of pupil diameter and response dynamics. Sensitive to cognitive load, emotional arousal, attention, and interest.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Robust correlations with cognitive workload and emotional response.

instruments.reference_apa: Duchowski, A. T. (2007). Eye Tracking Methodology: Theory and Practice (2nd ed.). Springer Science+Business Media.
instruments.description: Corneal reflection or electrooculography (EOG) system measuring gaze location, fixation duration, saccades, and pursuit. Maps visual attention and cognitive processing patterns.

psychometrics.validity_notes: High spatial and temporal resolution; validated against cortical visual processing.

instruments.authors: Ogawa, S., Lee, T. M., Kay, A. R., & Tank, D. W.
instruments.reference_apa: Ogawa, S., Lee, T. M., Kay, A. R., & Tank, D. W. (1990). Brain magnetic resonance imaging with contrast dependent on blood oxygenation. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 87(24), 9868-9872.
instruments.description: Non-invasive neuroimaging measuring blood oxygenation-level-dependent (BOLD) signal changes in response to cognitive tasks. High spatial resolution (mm scale) of brain activation patterns.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Excellent spatial localization; temporal resolution limited to seconds.

instruments.reference_apa: Luck, S. J. (2014). An Introduction to the Event-Related Potential Technique (2nd ed.). MIT Press.
instruments.description: Scalp electrode measurement of brain electrical activity. Continuous temporal resolution at millisecond precision; frequency domain analysis (delta, theta, alpha, beta, gamma bands).

psychometrics.validity_notes: Excellent temporal resolution; spatial resolution limited (volume conduction problem).

instruments.reference_apa: Jöbsis, F. F. (1977). Noninvasive infrared monitoring of cerebral and myocardial oxygen sufficiency and circulatory parameters. Science, 198(4323), 1264-1267.
instruments.description: Optical imaging measuring hemoglobin oxygenation in cortical tissue. Intermediate temporal (sub-second) and spatial resolution between EEG and fMRI.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Convergent validity with fMRI in prefrontal regions.

instruments.reference_apa: Luck, S. J. (2014). An Introduction to the Event-Related Potential Technique (2nd ed.). MIT Press.
instruments.description: Time-locked EEG averages aligned to stimulus events (e.g., P300, N400, MMN). Millisecond temporal resolution of cognitive processes with component decomposition.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Excellent temporal precision; individual differences in latency and amplitude vary.

instruments.authors: Basser, P. J., Mattiello, J., & LeBihan, D.
instruments.reference_apa: Basser, P. J., Mattiello, J., & LeBihan, D. (1994). MR diffusion tensor spectroscopy and imaging. Biophysical Journal, 66(1), 259-267.
instruments.description: Diffusion-weighted MRI measuring white matter tract organization and integrity. Provides information on structural connectivity and fiber orientation.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Good inter-site reliability; sensitive to white matter pathology.

instruments.reference_apa: International Electrotechnical Commission. (2013). Electroacoustics - Sound level meters (IEC 61672-1:2013). IEC.
instruments.description: Calibrated acoustic instrument measuring sound pressure level in decibels (dB) weighted to A-scale (dB(A)) to approximate human auditory sensitivity.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Excellent reliability; A-weighting approximates but does not fully capture psychoacoustic effects.

weaknesses: Ignores temporal variation and tonal character

instruments.full_name: ISO Technical Specification 15666 Noise Annoyance Index
instruments.reference_apa: International Standards Organization. (2003). Acoustics - Assessment of noise annoyance by means of social and socio-acoustic surveys (ISO/TS 15666:2003). ISO.
instruments.description: Standardized protocol and questionnaire for assessing noise annoyance in populations. Psychoacoustic framework linking physical sound properties to perceptual response.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates with epidemiological health outcomes related to noise.

instruments.reference_apa: International Commission on Illumination. (2018). CIE Handbook on Photometry and Related Data. CIE.
instruments.description: Calibrated light meter measuring illuminance (lux = lumens per square meter). Objective quantification of task lighting and ambient light levels.

psychometrics.validity_notes: High precision; photopic response approximates human luminosity function.

weaknesses: Does not capture color temperature effects

instruments.reference_apa: International Commission on Illumination. (2004). CIE 15:2004 Colorimetry (3rd ed.). CIE.
instruments.description: Spectral radiometer or colorimeter measuring correlated color temperature (CCT in Kelvin) and chromaticity. Characterizes light spectrum quality relevant to circadian and mood effects.

psychometrics.validity_notes: CCT correlates with melanopic lux and circadian photoentrainment.

instruments.reference_apa: Benedikt, M. L. (1979). To take hold of space. In W. Preiser (Ed.), Environmental Design Research, Vol. 1: Selected Papers (pp. 125-135). Dowden, Hutchinson & Ross.
instruments.description: Geometric analysis of all visible surfaces from observer position in 3D space. Quantifies spatial configuration properties like visual enclosure, complexity, and depth.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates with perceived enclosure (r ≈ 0.60) and spatial experience.

instruments.authors: Li, X., Ratti, C., & Seiferling, I.
instruments.reference_apa: Li, X., Ratti, C., & Seiferling, I. (2015). Mapping the sub-pixel density of green space using high resolution satellite image. Computers, Environment and Urban Systems, 54, 183-195.
instruments.description: Computational analysis quantifying visible green vegetation from a point location (percentage of green pixels in hemispherical image). Extended isovist integrating vegetation/naturalness.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Strong correlations with perceived naturalness and restorative quality (r > 0.70).

instruments.authors: Hagerhall, C. M., Purcell, T., & Taylor, R. P.
instruments.reference_apa: Hagerhall, C. M., Purcell, T., & Taylor, R. P. (2004). Fractal dimension of landscape silhouette outlines as a predictor of landscape preference. Journal of Environmental Psychology, 24(2), 247-255.
instruments.description: Mathematical analysis of self-similarity across scales in spatial patterns (e.g., tree silhouettes, building facades). Fractal dimension (D ≈ 1.0-1.5) predicts aesthetic preference.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Moderate correlations with perceived beauty and complexity (r = 0.40-0.65).

instruments.reference_apa: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. (2010). Guide to Indoor Air Quality. EPA.
instruments.description: Calibrated non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) sensor measuring CO2 concentration (ppm). Marker of ventilation adequacy and indoor air quality; affects cognitive performance above 1000 ppm.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Cognitive impairment threshold well-established at elevated CO2 levels.

instruments.reference_apa: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. (2012). Guidelines for Particulate Matter Monitoring and Quality Assurance. EPA.
instruments.description: Calibrated optical particle counter measuring fine particulate matter (≤2.5 μm). Health-relevant air quality indicator correlated with cardiovascular and respiratory outcomes.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Strong epidemiological links to health outcomes.

instruments.reference_apa: International Electrotechnical Commission. (2011). Sound system equipment - Part 16: Objective rating of speech intelligibility by Speech Transmission Index (IEC 60268-16:2011). IEC.
instruments.description: Modulation transfer function analysis predicting speech intelligibility in a space. Combines room acoustics (reverberation, background noise) to estimate word intelligibility percentage.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Excellent prediction of actual speech intelligibility (r = 0.90+).

instruments.reference_apa: World Health Organization. (1998). Wellbeing Measures in Primary Health Care: The DepCare Project. WHO.
instruments.description: 5-item self-report measure of psychological well-being. Simple screening for depression and quality of life across global populations.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Excellent sensitivity (0.94) and specificity (0.77) for depression screening.

instruments.authors: Tennant, R., Hiller, L., Fishwick, R., Platt, S., Joseph, S., Weich, S., ... & Stewart-Brown, S.
instruments.reference_apa: Tennant, R., Hiller, L., Fishwick, R., Platt, S., Joseph, S., Weich, S., ... & Stewart-Brown, S. (2007). The Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Well-Being Scale (WEMWBS): Development and UK validation. Health and Quality of Life Outcomes, 5(1), 63.
instruments.description: 14-item scale assessing positive mental health and well-being (not deficiency). Evaluates functioning, relationships, purpose, and contentment.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Sensitive to positive intervention effects; distinct from depression.

instruments.authors: Ware, J. E., & Sherbourne, C. D.
instruments.reference_apa: Ware, J. E., & Sherbourne, C. D. (1992). The MOS 36-item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36): I. Conceptual framework and item selection. Medical Care, 30(6), 473-483.
instruments.description: 36-item measure of health-related quality of life across 8 domains: physical functioning, role-physical, bodily pain, general health, vitality, social functioning, role-emotional, mental health.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Extensively validated; responsive to health interventions.

instruments.reference_apa: Burge, S. P. (2004). Sick building syndrome. Occupational and Environmental Medicine, 61(2), 185-190.
instruments.description: Self-report checklist of symptoms associated with indoor environmental exposure (headache, eyes/nose/throat irritation, fatigue, difficulty concentrating). No objective reference to specific causation.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Symptom prevalence correlates with IAQ measures (CO2, PM, VOCs).

instruments.reference_apa: Andersson, U., & Furmark, T. (1998). Activation and mood in everyday contexts: A psychophysiological study. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 75(4), 1012-1025.
instruments.description: 40-item assessment of activation and energy in natural daily environments. Distinguishes tense arousal from energetic activation.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Discriminates activation dimensions; context-dependent mood effects.

instruments.authors: Aron, A., Aron, E. N., & Smollan, D.
instruments.reference_apa: Aron, A., Aron, E. N., & Smollan, D. (1992). Inclusion of other in the self scale and the structure of interpersonal closeness. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 63(4), 596-612.
instruments.description: Single-item pictorial measure of relationship closeness. Seven overlapping Venn diagrams represent self-other overlap from minimal to complete union.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates with relationship duration (r = 0.60) and satisfaction (r = 0.70).

instruments.authors: Carron, A. V., Widmeyer, W. N., & Brawley, L. R.
instruments.reference_apa: Carron, A. V., Widmeyer, W. N., & Brawley, L. R. (1985). The development of an instrument to assess cohesion in sports teams: The Group Environment Questionnaire. Journal of Sport Psychology, 7(3), 244-266.
instruments.description: 18-item multidimensional measure of group cohesion across task and social dimensions, with individual and group attraction subscales.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Predicts group performance (r = 0.40-0.60) and member satisfaction.

weaknesses: Sport context origins may limit generalization

instruments.reference_apa: Rotter, J. B. (1967). A new scale for the measurement of interpersonal trust. Journal of Personality, 35(4), 651-665.
instruments.description: 25-item measure of generalized trust beliefs about others' honesty and sincerity. Assesses interpersonal trust across contexts.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates with cooperative behavior and risk-taking in trust games.

instruments.authors: Berg, J., Dickhaut, J., & McCabe, K.
instruments.reference_apa: Berg, J., Dickhaut, J., & McCabe, K. (1995). Trust, reciprocity, and social history. Games and Economic Behavior, 10(1), 122-142.
instruments.description: Behavioral economics paradigm where participant (sender) allocates money to trustee, who receives triple amount and decides how much to return. Measures behavioral trust and trustworthiness.

psychometrics.validity_notes: First-mover allocation correlates with personality-based trust (r = 0.30-0.50).

instruments.reference_apa: Bales, R. F. (1950). Interaction Process Analysis: A Method for the Study of Small Groups. Addison-Wesley.
instruments.description: Systematic observational coding scheme categorizing group communication into 12 interaction types (4 positive socioemotional, 4 task-related, 4 negative socioemotional). Real-time or video-coded assessment.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Reliable inter-rater agreement when trained coders (r > 0.80).

instruments.reference_apa: Freedson, P. S., Melanson, E., & Sirard, J. (1998). Calibration of the Computer Science and Applications Inc. accelerometer. Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise, 30(5), 777-781.
instruments.description: Commercial wearable accelerometer (wrist or waist-worn) measuring movement intensity. Categorizes activity into sedentary, light, moderate, vigorous intensity.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Good convergence with doubly labeled water energy expenditure (r = 0.60-0.70).

instruments.authors: Craig, C. L., Marshall, A. L., Sjöström, M., et al.
instruments.reference_apa: Craig, C. L., Marshall, A. L., Sjöström, M., et al. (2003). International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ): 12-country reliability and validity. Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise, 35(8), 1381-1395.
instruments.description: 7-item self-report of physical activity intensity, duration, and frequency across work, transportation, household, and recreational domains. Short (9 items) and long (27 items) versions available.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Moderate agreement with accelerometers (r = 0.50-0.60).

instruments.authors: Lejuez, C. W., Read, J. P., Kahler, C. W., Richards, J. B., Ramsey, S. E., Stuart, G. L., ... & Brown, R. A.
instruments.reference_apa: Lejuez, C. W., Read, J. P., Kahler, C. W., Richards, J. B., Ramsey, S. E., Stuart, G. L., ... & Brown, R. A. (2002). Evaluation of a behavioral measure of risk taking: The Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART). Journal of Experimental Psychology: Applied, 8(2), 75-84.
instruments.description: Computerized task where participant inflates virtual balloon, earning money for each pump but risking loss if balloon pops. Measures risk tolerance and impulsivity in decision-making.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates with real-world risky behavior (substance use, reckless driving).

instruments.authors: Blais, A. R., & Weber, E. U.
instruments.reference_apa: Blais, A. R., & Weber, E. U. (2006). A domain-specific risk-taking (DOSPERT) scale for adult populations. Judgment and Decision Making, 1(1), 33-47.
instruments.description: 40-item assessment of risk-taking likelihood and perceived risk/benefit across five domains: financial, health/safety, recreational, social, ethical.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Domain specificity: financial decisions independent of social risk-taking (r = 0.10).

instruments.authors: Bechara, A., Damasio, A. R., Damasio, H., & Anderson, S. W.
instruments.reference_apa: Bechara, A., Damasio, A. R., Damasio, H., & Anderson, S. W. (1994). Insensitivity to future consequences following damage to human prefrontal cortex. Cognition, 50(1-3), 7-15.
instruments.description: Computerized task with four decks of cards varying in immediate rewards and penalties. Participant learns to prefer decks yielding net gains. Measures decision-making under uncertainty and reward/punishment sensitivity.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Sensitive to ventromedial prefrontal cortex lesions; sensitive to substance use impairments.

instruments.authors: Dosen, A. S., & Ostwald, M. J.
instruments.reference_apa: Dosen, A. S., & Ostwald, M. J. (2016). Evidence for prospect-refuge spatial biophilia. Journal of Architectural and Planning Research, 33(2), 89-107.
instruments.description: Scale measuring spatial properties related to Appleton's prospect-refuge theory. Assesses visual openness (prospect) and protective enclosure (refuge) in architectural spaces.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates with perceived safety and aesthetic preference (r = 0.50-0.70).

instruments.authors: Jorgensen, B. S., & Stedman, R. C.
instruments.reference_apa: Jorgensen, B. S., & Stedman, R. C. (2001). Sense of place as an attitude: Lakeshore owner attitudes toward water-level fluctuation in a recreational lake in upstate New York. Journal of Environmental Education, 32(4), 16-23.
instruments.description: Three-subscale measure (12 items total) of attachment to place, identity, and dependence on a specific environment. Assesses emotional bonds and place meanings.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Predicts environmental stewardship behavior (r = 0.60-0.80).

instruments.reference_apa: Purcell, T., & Lamb, R. J. (1998). Symbolic associations with landscape types in environmentally concerned groups. Journal of Environmental Psychology, 18(1), 41-53.
instruments.description: Scale measuring perception of naturalness in visual environments. Evaluates biophilic content, wildness, and lack of human modification.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Correlates with restorative quality and well-being effects (r = 0.70-0.80).

instruments.reference_apa: Paciuk, M. (1990). The role of personal control of the environment in thermal comfort and satisfaction at the workplace. Unpublished doctoral dissertation, Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm.
instruments.description: Scale measuring perceived control over thermal, acoustic, and lighting environment. Assesses both actual control capability and psychological sense of control.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Perceived control correlates with satisfaction independent of actual environmental conditions.

instruments.reference_apa: Lynch, K. (1960). The Image of the City. MIT Press.
instruments.description: Observational and cognitive mapping method assessing urban environmental legibility. Five elements (paths, edges, districts, nodes, landmarks) characterize spatial organization and navigability.

psychometrics.validity_notes: Cognitive mapping agreement predicts navigation wayfinding performance (r = 0.60-0.80).
